subject: Workplace Skills
title: Why People Pivot
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Why People Pivot.

hook.text: The Bureau of Labor Statistics says the average person changes careers four to seven times in their lifetime.

buildup.text: Pivots happen for many reasons: burnout, curiosity, market shifts, or simply outgrowing a role or industry.

discovery.text: Most pivots aren't leaps of faith. They're bridges between what you know and what you want to learn.

twist.text: Your existing skills transfer more than you think. A teacher's facilitation skills shine in corporate training.

climax.text: Map your transferable skills: communication, problem-solving, project management. These cross any industry boundary.

punchline.text: Skills transfer. Pivots are bridges, not cliffs.

quiz.question: What makes career pivots more achievable than people expect?
options: Employers don't care about previous experience
Existing skills often transfer well to new industries
Pivoting always leads to higher salaries
